newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling stable vs dlr, remains bullish.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling stable vs dlr, remains bullish.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling held its ground on Thursday on the back of heavy dollar inflows and low demand for the U.S. currency, dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 54.70 against the dollar from 54.71 on Wednesday, while against the pound it was posted at a mean rate of 89.29 from 88.49.
"Dollar demand is at record low levels," a dealer said.
Meantime Central Bank Deputy Governor Nzioki Kibua said the bank would welcome a weaker shilling to meet exporter concerns.

"The central bank would welcome an exchange rate (shilling) depreciation to address some of the tea exporters problems provided depreciation is supported with changes in economic fundamentals including inflation and balance of payments," Kibua told a meeting of tea growers in Kericho, western Kenya.
Another dealer said shilling gains this week were supported by heavy inflows from foreign investors and the coffee sector.
"A lot of people are squaring positions ahead of the long Easter break," he added.

Dealers said market sentiment seemed to favour a strong shilling in the short term if current low levels of demand prevailed. There was no immediate indication that the central bank planned to move into the market to force a shilling fall.
The money market was slightly short. Overnight rates were quoted unchanged at 15 percent.
